newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela inflation falls to 3.1 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela inflation falls to 3.1 pct in November.

text.p: Venezuela's inflation rate in November was 3.1 percent, down from 5.6 percent in November 1995 and 4.2 percent in October this year, the central bank said.
November's rate brought inflation over the past 12 months to 109.2 percent, compared to 52.9 percent in the twelve months to November 1995.

The drop returns inflation to a downward trend after the figure jumped in October following increases in electricity and telephone rates. It was broadly in line with government estimates and the lowest monthly rate since August 1995.

Inflation peaked at 12.6 percent in May, but has since fallen thanks to an IMF-supported economic reform program launched in April. The plan removed currency and interest rate controls and increased gasoline prices fivefold.
The Central Bank said in a release that price rises decelerated for all products and services apart from clothing and shoes which rose 4.8 percent.
Cumulative inflation for the first 11 months of the year now stands at 97.4 percent, compared to 47.7 percent over the same period last year.
Government officials have said they said they see inflation for the year coming in at between 95 and 100 percent, compared to 56.6 percent last year.
December inflation is expected at around two percent -- slightly above the government's target of 1.5 percent.
